questions.question: What is "Internet English"?
options: The distinctive ways English is used in digital contexts, including textspeak and informal styles
The official language of internet providers
questions.explanation: Internet English covers digital varieties of English: textspeak, abbreviations, emoji-supported writing, and platform-specific styles.

questions.question: What is digital code-switching?
options: Shifting your language style depending on the online context, like formal email versus casual chat
questions.explanation: Just as people speak differently to teachers and friends, they switch styles between formal emails, social media posts, and group chats.

questions.question: Where did textspeak abbreviations like "lol" and "brb" originate?
options: In character-limited and fast-paced digital messaging
questions.explanation: Textspeak developed for speed and character limits in SMS and chat - abbreviations, acronyms, and dropped punctuation.

questions.question: Has digital communication ruined the English language, according to linguists?
options: No - it has added new registers and styles; users still command formal language when needed
Yes - formal English no longer exists
Yes - young people can no longer write
No - because digital English is identical to formal English
questions.explanation: Research shows digital writing is an additional register, not a replacement: skilled users switch between informal chat style and formal writing.

questions.question: How do emoji function in digital communication?
options: They convey tone and emotion that body language and intonation provide in speech
questions.explanation: Emoji compensate for the absence of facial expressions and tone of voice in writing, signalling irony, warmth, or emphasis.
